chunks: From him, from Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Abd al-Rahman ibn Abi Najran, from Asim ibn Humayd, from Muhammad ibn Qays, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him), who said:

The Commander of the Faithful (peace be upon him) said: 'Any man who leaves behind a concubine who has a child, or is pregnant with a child, or has no child, if her master frees her, she is freed; and if he does not free her until he dies, the Book of Allah has preceded regarding her, and the Book of Allah is more entitled [to be followed]. If she has a child and he leaves wealth, she is placed in the share of her child.'

He said: 'The Commander of the Faithful (peace be upon him) ruled in the case of a man who left behind a girl who had borne him a daughter, and she was a minor but could distinguish speech, so she freed her mother; and the patrons of the girl's father disputed over her, so he validated her freeing her mother.'

key_terms.أَمِيرُ الْمُؤْمِنِينَ: Commander of the Faithful (Ali ibn Abi Talib)
key_terms.أُمّ الْوَلَد: Concubine who bears her master a child

ai.seo_question: What is the legal status of a concubine who has a child with her master after his death?
ai.summary: This hadith from Imam al-Sadiq (AS) clarifies the status of the *umm al-walad* (concubine who bears a child) upon her master's death, establishing that her emancipation is divinely mandated if not executed during his lifetime, thereby integrating her into the inheritance structure as the child's share. The narrative highlights the jurisprudential authority of Imam Ali (AS) in validating the emancipation of a minor daughter who possessed sufficient legal capacity (*tamyiz*), resolving disputes among the master's patrons (*mawali*) by prioritizing the Quranic principle of emancipation. This ruling underscores the Shia legal emphasis on the automatic liberation of the mother and the child's right to inherit her share, reflecting the broader Quranic ethic of freeing slaves.
